A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their full main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A-H are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original counting and color experiments on three VLMs, including attention-head ablations, probability and attention analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds random-head ablation controls and evaluations on CalTech101, MM-Vet, and POPE.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D retain the same mean-ablation procedure, ranking by correction success, and grouped head selection: three heads for Qwen-VL and ten for LLaVA-OneVision and Janus-Pro. The identified heads and their use on the color task are unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained CountBench counting and Visual CounterFact color tasks, v2 adds image-conditioned sentence repetition on CalTech101, multimodal question answering covering recognition, OCR, spatial and knowledge reasoning on MM-Vet, and object-existence questions on POPE. This substantially broadens evaluated task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds randomly selected head ablations to the existing counting comparisons, matching the number and layers of the PIH heads. v1 compared only the unablated models with PIH-head ablation; those comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce a control matched by head count and layer, a CalTech101 conditional sentence-copying protocol, and before/after evaluations on MM-Vet and POPE. The original counting and color protocols, sample filtering, generation limit, and head-selection settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds focused checks of whether hallucination reductions are specific to selected heads and whether ablation disrupts useful copying or broader capabilities. Existing extreme-offset tests, head-count sensitivity, attention analyses, and qualitative examples in the appendices are retained.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged. The new random-head and capability results provide point estimates without adding run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The revision substantially extends reported outcomes. Table 1 adds random-ablation prompt-match rates of 37.80, 54.60, and 58.30 for LLaVA-OV, Qwen-VL, and Janus-Pro, versus retained PIH-ablation rates of 1.42, 3.22, and 10.19. New Table 2 reports capability results with both gains and losses. Original counting, color, and appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mean-ablation equations in Appendix D and definitions of copying forms are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no new formal assumptions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about localized PIH mechanisms, mitigation without training, transfer to color prediction, and preserved general performance. The added evaluations support an existing claim rather than introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 interprets the capability evaluations as broadly stable performance without negative side effects, extending the discussion beyond counting. This interpretation is stronger than the mixed scores alone establish. Existing mechanism explanations and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 documents the exact CalTech101 repetition prompt and the head-count and layer-matching rules for the new random control. Existing hardware, checkpoint, resource, generation, and code-access disclosures remain unchanged. Detailed sample selection and scoring procedures for the added benchmarks are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for CalTech101 (Li et al., 2022), POPE (Li et al., 2023), and MM-Vet (Yu et al., 2023) alongside their evaluations. The related-work discussion and positioning of the main contribution otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts Section 4.3, renumbers the former Section 4.3 as 4.4, makes Limitations unnumbered, adds acknowledgments, and updates contact information and some wording. Most existing prose and the appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains random-control rows; new Tables 2 and 3 display capability results and a styled summary of previously reported heads. The color table becomes full-width, the response-format table changes model order, and appendix displays are relocated. All ten figure images are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's evidence with a matched random-head control showing much smaller hallucination reductions, and directly tests the existing claim of preserved capabilities. These are useful but limited gains: the new evaluations lack uncertainty and detailed protocols, while the claim of no negative side effects is insufficiently qualified given declines such as Qwen-VL's CalTech101 score from 100.0 before ablation to 96.0 after.
